items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions George Handy; Interviewee responds 'Right. I did them for McKinley... They didn't even do them in Sauter-Finegan.' and later 'And for Pete Rugolo too.'

ctx.x: it. So why knock yourself out on something that he's not going to use. I remember why I left Benny. I left Benny because I couldn't hear anymore. I couldn't hear G or C. In order to do what I was doing, there was just too much repeti- tion and I needed stimulation of another sort at that time.

In that Metronome interview, it is interesting, especially for me since I had that involvement with that Boyd Raeburn project recently, you mention in there that George Handy, who at the time was writing for the Raeburn band and was doing really, quite a few adventurous things, you mentioned that he was doing the things for Boyd that you'd really not had a chance to do with the bands that you worked with.
Right. I did them for McKinley, but he didn't play them either. Not those. They didn't even do them in Sauter-Finegan.
